findings.evidence: Post-merge P1 on PR #438 / Issue #436: raw task_text below the ingress byte ceiling expanded beyond the available budget after the machine rendered JSON/spec/context, yet the build still received an automation envelope and could proceed toward handoff/dispatch. The ingress now drains the canonical compiled outcome and raises PromptTaskUnreadyError for any non-READY build or missing prompt artifact, and the P1 reproduction proves no fallback dispatch and no DISPATCHED/COMPLETED ledger state on the failure.

Fixing the P1 might have introduced a second renderer or a duplicate budget authority that re-measures rendered size instead of accepting the machine's own outcome. The gate reads allocation.outcome and manifest.prompt_artifact_id directly from the PromptCompilationResult the machine produced; no parallel renderer or duplicate pricing exists, and the source regression still pins both production callers through the one ingress.

Raw-size-only validation could recur elsewhere in the engineering surface. DFF-018 is added with scope src/hunter/evidence_intelligence/ and deterministic fail-closed regressions, and the preflight guard recomputes applicable families from changed paths on every push, so any future engineering ingress path that bypasses the compiled-outcome gate is review-blocked.

A fail-closed rejection without a deterministic machine-readable reason would leave callers and automation unable to distinguish INSUFFICIENT_BUDGET from other non-READY outcomes. PromptTaskUnreadyError carries ENGINEERING_TASK_NOT_READY key=value text plus structured fields, and the deterministic identity of the reason across repeated compiles is asserted.
